_comment: The Dwarf voice (NPCConversation II.1b, SpeciesVoice). speech: the rules run over any shared line they say. voice: openers and closers. thought: their own thoughts by situation. script: two-person scripts, speaker 0 is always the Dwarf.

openers: As my grandfather used to say,
Between you, me and the anvil,
I will say this once, and slowly:
Down in the halls we say,
closers: That is dwarf wisdom, free of charge.
And that is the end of it.
My grandfather said so, and he was never wrong.
Nothing built in a hurry, mind.
Write it down. No, carve it.
As sure as the deep halls.
Take it or leave it, but take it.

generic: The mortar on this street is {crumbling|rotten|a disgrace}. Somebody should be ashamed.
Iron prices up again. {My anvil weeps|My purse weeps|Everybody weeps}.
Must sharpen the {chisels|axe|kitchen knives} tonight. They have gone dull with shame.
A grudge kept warm is a grudge kept well.
This town's beer is {thin|cloudy|criminal}. I will drink it anyway. Out of politeness.
Who built that balcony? It is held up by hope and two nails.
My beard has a knot in it. I will not rest until it is out.
My forge was cold this morning. I took it personally.
A good door should shut with one sound, not three.
{Granite|Basalt|Marble} on the church steps. Somebody here once had taste.
I have been chewing on this problem for {three days|a week|eleven years}. It is nearly soft.
Tall folk keep patting my head. I keep a list.
Nothing worth having was ever made in a hurry. Except beer. Beer is urgent.
The new bridge sings in the wind. Bridges should not sing.
I can hear a {loose bolt|cracked bell|bad hinge} from across the square. Curse of the trade.
My apprentice used glue again. We will be having words.
Stone remembers. That is why I talk to it kindly.
Thinkering on a new lock. {Seven|Nine|Thirteen} pins. Nobody will open it, including me.
A song for the hammer: one strike per word. My songs are short.
These chairs are built for giants. My feet have not touched the floor all day.
My cousin wrote from the mines. The seam runs {deeper|richer|stranger} than anyone thought.
A dwarf forgives. A dwarf also writes it down, just in case.
Somebody painted over good oak. I may never recover.
I need a pint and a problem, in that order.
Valkyrie drill at dawn. {My shield arm|My back|My pride} still aches from yesterday.
The guard roster has me on nights again. Good. The night is honest.
Polished my helmet. I can see my beard in it. Magnificent.
The tram rails here are badly laid. I could do it with my eyes shut.
Nobody hums while they work anymore. The work can tell.
My grandfather's anvil is three hundred years old and still rings true. Like him.
{One more|Just one|A final} pint and then home. The usual lie.
Gnomes make things clever. Dwarves make things last. Elves make things pretty. Guess who gets paid.
Wrote to the town council about that drain. My {fourth|ninth|twelfth} letter.
Coal smoke in the air. Somebody is working. Good.
My knees know the weather before the radio does.
The best hammer is the one your hand forgets it is holding.
Somebody whistled at my beard. I will take it as a compliment. Then as a grudge.
I dreamt of hinges again. Perfect, silent hinges.
A crack in the wall is a story. This wall has written a novel.
Earned {forty|sixty|ninety} euros mending pots today. Honest money, sooty hands.

sleep: My eyelids weigh more than an anvil. Bed.
Awake since {the first shift|the cock crowed|the forge was lit}. Enough.
Need sleep. Somewhere low, dark and quiet. Like a cellar.
I nearly nodded off into my beer. That is a crime against beer.
Even stone gets tired. Well, no. But I do.
Bed, and a pillow under the beard. Nothing more.
hunger: Hungry enough to eat {a roast|a whole ham|a cart of sausages}.
My stomach is grumbling louder than I do. That takes effort.
Dark bread and hard cheese. That is all I ask of this world.
Cannot work on an empty belly. The hammer knows.
Something with gravy. Anything with gravy.
If I do not eat soon I will start holding grudges against food.
work: Back to the forge. The {horseshoes|hinges|blades} will not shape themselves.
Idle hands rust. Time to work.
Shift starts soon. Boots laced, beard tucked.
A day without work is a day without a story.
That commission is overdue. Overdue is a dirty word.
I can hear my workbench calling. It sounds hurt.
leisure: An evening off. A pint, a pipe, a song.
Even an anvil gets Sundays off. Mostly.
Time for darts. I throw like I hammer: hard and straight.
I should do something for fun. Carving counts. Carving always counts.
A long song in a low room. That is what I need.
Too much work makes a dwarf {a boulder|a grump|a bore}.
crime: That merchant cheated my cousin in 1987. His window is right there... No. Grudges are for books.
That lock is shoddy work. I could open it with {a spoon|a hairpin|a harsh word}. I will not.
Nobody guards that tool shed. Lovely chisels in there. Lovely, unguarded chisels.
A dwarf takes what is owed. Is it owed? Let me check the book.
That purse is heavy. Heavier than my conscience? Close.
Shoddy door, cheap hinge, nobody home. It is practically an invitation.
hygiene: My beard smells of {soot|onions|three different taverns}. Bath.
Soot to the elbows. Time to scrub.
I found yesterday's lunch in my beard. Enough.
Need a wash, and the comb, and the good beard oil.
I smell like a forge. Lovely to me, less to others.
Dust from the mine in every crease. Hot water, please.
money: {Eight|Twelve|Twenty} euros until payday. Iron does not buy itself.
Purse is light. A dwarf with a light purse is a dwarf in a bad mood.
Someone still owes me for that gate. It is in the book.
Need coin. Could take on a few repair jobs. Pots, locks, anything.
Gold in the hills and nothing in my pocket. The world is badly arranged.
Counted my savings twice. They did not grow. Counted a third time anyway.
safety: Something is off on this street. My beard is bristling.
Hand on the hammer. Just in case.
Too many shadows, too few walls. I want stone around me.
Heard {boots|shouting|glass breaking} behind me. Not turning round. Yet.
Feet planted, back to the wall. Old guard habit.
If goblins come, they come through me first. Short, but wide.
comfort: My chair at home was cut to my height. Everything here is cut for herons.
Miss my hearth. Miss my slippers. Miss my anvil, oddly most of all.
A low ceiling and a thick wall. That is all comfort is.
This room is too {draughty|tall|bright}. Give me a cellar.
A warm fire and boots off. Is that so much to ask?
My back wants a proper bench, not this wobbly elf-built thing.
social: Nobody to argue with for {two days|a week|too long}. I am going soft.
Need a crowded table and somebody to out-sing.
Should visit my cousins. They will have new grudges to share.
A pint alone is just a drink. A pint with friends is a feast.
Been talking to my hammer again. It is a good listener, but dull.
Somebody, anybody, come and tell me I am wrong. I miss it.

rain: Rain. Now we see what {the gutters|the drains|the roof tiles} of this town are worth.
Rain on the forge roof. Best music there is.
Wet beard, wet boots, wet mood.
Rain. Stone loves rain. Iron does not. I am torn.
Good day for the workshop. Bad day for whoever built that leaky roof.
Rain finds every crack. That is how you learn where the cracks are.
storm: Thunder! Sounds like the old halls on a feast day.
Lightning likes tall things. One more reason to be short.
Storm. Shutters down, fire up, ale out.
That roof will not last the night. I said so {in spring|in March|in writing}.
The wind is testing every weld in town. Let us see who did honest work.
A storm is just the sky swinging a hammer.
snow: Snow. Like home in the high passes. Almost.
Snow up to my knees. Which is not very much snow, to be fair.
Cold iron sticks to the fingers. Gloves today.
Snow on the beard. Very distinguished.
Snowed in? Good. Mulled ale and a long story.
Shovelled {the path|the steps|the whole street} before anyone woke. Nobody thanked me. Noted.
clear: Clear sky. Good light for fine work.
Sun on the stone. The whole town looks warmer, even the ugly bits.
Clear day. You can see the mountains. I always look.
Too much sun for a dwarf. I will find shade under an arch.
Bright day. Perfect for {drying hides|airing the forge|a beer outside}.
Dry weather. Mortar sets well today. Good day to build.

morning: Morning. Forge lit before sunrise, as it should be.
Dawn. My beard is still asleep, the rest of me is working.
Porridge, strong tea, cold water on the face. Ready.
Morning shift. The best hammering is done before anyone complains.
Early. The streets belong to bakers and dwarves.
Woke before the {rooster|bells|baker}. As usual. Smug about it.
afternoon: Afternoon. The work is half done and the beer is half earned.
Sun is high. My shadow is the same size as me, for once.
Lunch settling. The hammer feels heavier after lunch.
Afternoon lull. Good time for fine filing.
Halfway through the day and only one argument so far. Slow day.
Long afternoon. I will {mend a chair|sharpen something|nap on a sack}.
evening: Evening. Fire banked, tools hung, tankard found.
The tavern lights are on. My feet know the way.
Evening. Time to polish the grudges.
Sunset on the hills. Somewhere under them, ore is sleeping.
End of the shift. My hands smell of iron and honest sweat.
Evening song time. Low voices, long verses.
night: Night. Quiet as a mineshaft. I like it.
Night watch. Lantern, axe, flask of tea. Mostly tea.
Dark. Dwarves see well enough in the dark. We just do not brag.
Late. Still thinking about that hinge. It will not let me sleep.
Night. The stars look like sparks off a big anvil.
{Midnight|Past one|Nearly two}. Last pint. Truly the last. Probably.

SPRING: Spring. The thaw finds every bad roof in town.
Mountain passes open again. Letters from home soon.
Spring. The young ones are dancing. I am supervising, with ale.
Mud season. Boots twice as heavy, temper too.
SUMMER: Summer. A forge in summer is a punishment for old sins.
Hot. Even my beard is sweating.
Summer. Cold cellar, cold beer, closed door.
Long days. Good light for long work.
Summer fair in town. I will judge the metalwork stalls. Harshly.
AUTUMN: Autumn. Brewing season. The best season.
Leaves falling. Time to check the chimney before winter checks it for me.
Autumn. Wood stacked, coal ordered, grudges sorted.
Harvest beer is in. My heart is full, my tankard fuller.
Autumn wind in the beard. Feels like the old country.
WINTER: Winter. The forge is the warmest place in town. Everyone visits.
Long nights, long songs, long beards. Dwarf season.
Ice on the tools. Bring them in, warm them up, apologise.
Winter feast soon. I have been growing my appetite since autumn.
Frost on the windows. Pretty, like elf work. Gone by noon, like elf work.

poor: Bread and dripping again. Honest food for an honest purse.
Mended my boots a {third|fifth|seventh} time. They are more patch than boot.
Sold my second hammer. A dwarf with one hammer is half a dwarf.
No coin for coal. Cold forge, cold heart.
Poor, aye. But nobody can say my work is poor.
Water instead of ale tonight. My ancestors are turning in their cairns.
comfortable: Enough for coal, enough for ale, a little for the good beard oil. Plenty.
Steady work, steady pay. Like a steady hammer.
Bought new tongs. Not needed. Wanted. That is comfort.
Rent paid, larder full, grudges up to date. A good month.
Put a little aside for {a new anvil|my nephew's apprenticeship|a barrel of good ale}.
Not rich. Not poor. Solid. Like a good wall.
rich: Commissioned a gold-inlaid tankard. For myself. Every dwarf deserves one.
Bought the whole mine. Well, a share. A big share.
Rich enough to pay off my grudges. Not going to. Grudges are not for sale.
My vault door is a metre of steel. I forged it myself. Twice.
Bought a round for the whole tavern. {Twice|Three times|All night}.
Varlenia folk keep inviting me to dinner. They want my vault door, not my company.

familiar: Those travellers again. I {remember them well|had not forgotten|never forget} faces like theirs.
Ah, the ones with the van. They owe me nothing. Yet.
Back again? Good. Familiar faces are like old tools: they fit the hand.
Those folk. They paid fair last time. That goes in the good book.
I know that lot. One of them leans on my walls.
The travellers! Somebody put the kettle on. And the ale.
Them again. A dwarf never forgets a face, or a debt, or a kindness.
There they are. Still in one piece, I see. Mostly.
Those wanderers. Their boots look worse each time. I could fix them.
Familiar faces. I will nod. A dwarf nod is worth a hug from anyone else.
hordeGround: Horde ground. They have pulled down good stone walls to build ugly ones.
Goblin banners on a dwarf-built bridge. My grandfather would weep.
The Horde does not keep grudges. It keeps everything else.
Horde land. Hammer close, mouth shut, eyes open.
I am writing every goblin I see into the book. I will need a bigger book.
Their forges burn too hot and too fast. Everything they make cracks by spring.
They paint everything. Paint hides bad work. I would know.
One shared head, they say. I would like a word with it.
Horde ground. Keep the beard tucked. They grab.
Even here the mountains are not theirs. Mountains belong to nobody, and a little to dwarves.
abroad: Far from the halls. The beer here is a foreign concept, in every sense.
They build with brick here. Brick! Like bread for walls.
Nobody here has heard of my family. Their loss.
A long way from home. My boots know every mile of it.
Foreigners keep asking if the beard is real. Pull it and see. Gently.
Wrote home. Told them the stone here is soft and the people softer.
Abroad, a dwarf is a rumour. I am happy to be a solid one.
The locals here are kind. Kind, and very tall.
No dwarf hall for {a hundred|three hundred|five hundred} kilometres. I am the hall now.
Strange land, strange food, same hammer. Everything is fine.

forge: A dwarf child's first word is often 'hot'. Forge children learn fast.
We name our anvils. Mine is called Patience. She is not.
A blade takes {a hundred|a thousand|ten thousand} strikes. A reputation takes one bad one.
Thinkerers are dwarves who forge ideas. Most of them explode. Some of them fly.
The fire in the old hall has not gone out in four hundred years. Someone always stays.
Never quench in anger. The steel remembers.
The Mages' Guild buys our steel for their staff caps. They never ask how. We never tell.
A master's mark is tiny and hidden. If you have to show it, the work was not good enough.
deep: Deep down, the stone is warm and it hums. Miners say it is the world thinking.
Since 1992, some tunnels come out somewhere they did not go in. We mark those with red chalk.
Every miner knows the canary. Ours sing in harmony.
Never whistle in a mine. The mountain thinks you are mocking it.
My grandmother found a seam of {silver|blue quartz|something nameless} that hummed in two dimensions at once.
Under the Alps there are halls older than any map. We do not draw them on maps.
Stone tells you where it will break, if you listen. Most people do not listen.
A cave-in is the mountain changing its mind. You respect that, and you dig faster.
grudges: My family's grudge book runs to {eleven|fourteen|twenty} volumes. Volume one is mostly about a goat.
A grudge is crossed out only when the debt is paid. Some of the ink is three hundred years old.
We do not hate. We remember precisely. It is different.
Grandfather held a grudge against a bridge for forty years. The bridge fell first.
There is a page in the book for the Horde. It is a very long page.
Forgiving is allowed. Forgetting is not. That is the whole rule.
My aunt crossed out a grudge on her deathbed. The family still talks about it.
A good grudge makes you work harder. Spite has built more halls than gold.
ale: Every hall has its own yeast. Ours came over the mountains in a beard. Do not ask.
A wedding needs three barrels: one for the guests, one for the family, one for the arguments.
Ale is liquid bread. Bread is solid ale. The cycle is sacred.
We toast the dead with dark ale and the newborn with light. Everyone in between gets what is left.
Never brew in a hurry. Hurried ale tastes like regret.
My uncle brewed a stout so thick you could {stand a spoon|float a coin|drive a nail} in it.
Valkyries drink last at the feast. It is an honour. They pretend it is not a hardship.
A singer drinks free in any hall. That is why we have so many singers.
beards: A beard is a record. Every braid is a deed, every bead a promise.
Cutting a dwarf's beard is a crime in three countries and a war in a fourth.
My first braid was for my first hinge. I was {nine|eleven|twelve}.
Valkyries braid steel wire into theirs. It stops a sword. It has also stopped a wedding.
Beard oil recipes are family secrets. Ours has juniper and something we do not name.
Clean-shaven dwarves exist. We are polite about it. Mostly.
Tuck your beard near machines. Every dwarf learns this exactly once.
A grey beard is not old. A grey beard is seasoned, like good timber.
squishing: Varlenia appeared in one night in January. Nothing built in a night can be trusted. Not even a continent.
The Rule of 80: nothing faster than eighty an hour. Dwarves obeyed it for centuries before it existed.
That Omega tower goes down further than it goes up, they say. I would love to see its footings.
Ninety-two dimensions, squeezing together since 1992. Somewhere, a very bad mason is responsible.
A time bubble swallowed a quarry near us. The same block gets cut every morning, forever.
That Liminal Engine folds the road. Clever. I would never ride in it. I would take it apart, though.
Rich folk moved to Varlenia by the boatload. Let them. Its stone has no memory.
Since the Squishing, some ores turn up from {other worlds|nowhere|tomorrow}. They ring wrong on the anvil.

positive: {b}! I fixed your gate. It squeaked. I could not bear it.
You didn't have to do that, {a}. Thank you.
I did have to. The squeak was personal.
First round is on me, {b}. Second one too.
What's the occasion?
You paid me back on time. That earns a dwarf's respect and two pints.
I made you something. A knife. Do not argue.
It's beautiful. Look at the handle!
Ash wood, oiled three times. It will outlive both of us.
Then I'll leave it to someone in my will.
You remembered my grandfather's name, {b}. Nobody remembers.
You told the story four times. It stuck.
Four times! Then you are practically family.
Your new shelf is level. I checked. I was impressed.
Coming from you, that's something.
It is everything. Do not let it go to your head.
Sing with me, {b}. The old mining song.
I don't know the words.
Nobody knows the words. That is not the point of the song.
Fine. Loudly, then.
I am crossing you out of the book, {b}.
What book?
The grudge book. That business with the ladder. Forgiven.
I didn't even know I was in it!
Since 1996. Do not worry. It was a small entry.
Your bread is good, {b}. Heavy. Honest.
Heavy is a compliment?
From a dwarf, heavy is the highest compliment there is.
negative: You used nails on that oak, {b}. Nails.
It's a fence, not a cathedral.
Everything is a cathedral if you do it right.
So is a grudge, at first.
That knife I sold you. You used it as a screwdriver.
It worked. It did not work fine. There is a difference.
You still owe me for the hinges, {b}. Six months now.
I said I'd pay you next week.
You said that in the spring. I wrote it down.
I put my coffee on it for a second.
A second is all it takes to lose a friend.
Your beer is thin, {b}, and your tap is crooked.
I would, if anywhere else were better. That is what makes me angry.
neutral: Excuse me. Who laid these cobbles?
The council, I think. Years ago.
Tell the council a dwarf noticed. They will know what that means.
Is there a smithy in this town?
Down by the river. Old Marco runs it.
Is old Marco any good?
He's the only one.
That is not what I asked.
Your door is out of true, you know.
It shuts, doesn't it?
It shuts. It does not shut properly. Good day.
Which way to the tram stop?
Straight on, then left at the bakery.
A bakery. Good. That makes two stops, then.
Weather is turning.
Is it? The sky looks clear.
My knees disagree with the sky. My knees are usually right.
How much for the iron pan?
Twelve euros.
Hm. *taps it* Eleven, and I will not mention the casting flaw.
Done.
Is that a chess set? Who carved it?
My father, a long time ago.
Then your father had good hands. Tell him a dwarf said so.
Does this tavern have a low stool?
We have a crate.
A crate. Well. I have sat on worse thrones.
Seen the news? They are building a new bridge on the ring road.
About time, the old one shakes.
The new one will shake too. Mark my words. They are rushing it.
Good morning. Is this the queue for the post office?
It is. It's been the queue since nine.
Good. I am patient. I am built for queues.
Are {those mountains|those hills|those peaks} to the north mined?
There was a quarry once. It closed.
Closed. Hmph. Nothing is ever finished with a mountain, only interrupted.
Is it always this loud in this square?
Market day. It's worse on Saturdays.
Good. Noise means trade. Trade means work. Work means beer.

lines: Machines will never replace a smith's hands.
Factories make a thousand nails an hour.
A thousand bad nails. I make twelve good ones.
And I need a thousand.
Things should be built to last a hundred years.
Agreed. My grandmother's table is still the best thing in the house.
There. That is how a table should be.
Varlenia should not be trusted. It appeared overnight.
It's a whole continent. People live there now.
People lived in Pompeii too.
That's not the same thing at all!
A grudge is just memory with a sense of duty.
Ha! My mother would agree with you.
Your mother sounds like a wise woman.
Magic is a craft, like smithing. Practice and calluses.
Magic is a gift. Some people just have it.
Nobody just has anything. They practised where you could not see.
The best beer is brewed slowly.
No argument there. The fast stuff tastes like tin.
Tin! Exactly. Let me buy you a slow one.

ambient: I can smell it from here.
Mind the step, it is cracked.
Every day's long at the bench.
Hinge on your shutter needs oil.
That bell is cracked, you know.
I always thought it sounded odd.
